title: Mid-Term Plan Switches — Installment Payment Plans
content:
**Targets and count.** Under the **Installment Payment Plans**, a plan is switched only to a plan listed among its switch targets, and the switches already used in the term must be below the plan's allowance.

**Switching onto automatic draft.** A switch to a Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan requires a recurring payment authorization signed by the customer at least the plan's authorization lead time (3 calendar days) before the next draft date. The customer personally signs a recurring payment authorization, stating the last four digits of the account or card; that statement comes from the customer, while the signing date and the switch targets are read from the plan's records. A plan restricted to certified funds can never be switched to a Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan.

**Switching to Paid-in-Full.** A switch to the Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan is made only when the whole account balance is paid, and future installment fees are then avoided.

**Unbilled installments — base clause, no longer in force as written.** The base sentence "unbilled installments keep their amounts and due dates; invoices issued after the switch carry the new plan's installment fee" is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis: for a move of a plan billing an Owner Auto Policy term off automatic draft to the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan that the named insured asks for under the move's schedule, and only for such a move, the scheduled premium not yet invoiced, less the switch down payment the move took, is spread again in equal shares over the installments not yet invoiced, which keep their due dates, the last absorbing any rounding difference; that respread installment premium is what every later invoice of the moved plan bills as its installment premium under the base installment schedule, the first invoice after the move carries the fee that schedule sets and every later invoice carries the new plan's installment fee; on any other switch, a plan the returned-draft or certified-funds rules move to the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan included, unbilled installments keep their amounts and due dates and invoices issued after the switch carry the new plan's installment fee.

**Hypothetical points of judgement**

- A Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan customer asks to move to the Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan: not a switch target of that plan.
- A Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan customer whose next draft date would be the 12th signs an EFT authorization on the 9th: 3 calendar days before, in time.
- A plan flagged for certified funds asks to move to the Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan: never allowed.

superseded_clauses: Unbilled installments keep their amounts and due dates; invoices issued after the switch carry the new plan's installment fee.
